    Write a number or short text to your Overleaf project

    write_overleaf_tex.Rd

    Writes a single value - usually a key statistic - to a .tex file in your Overleaf project's atlas folder, ready to include in the report with \input{atlas/filename}. Designed to sit at the end of a pipe that pull()s out one number.

    write_overleaf_tex(value, filename, accuracy = NULL, push = TRUE)

    Arguments

    value

    A single value: a number, or text that is already formatted. Numbers are written in full (1000000, never 1e+06) unless you supply accuracy.

    filename

    Name of the file to write in the atlas folder, with or without the .tex extension. Can include a subfolder, such as "stats/debt-2025".

    accuracy

    Optional. Round a number to this accuracy before writing it, using scales::number() with a comma between thousands - so accuracy = 0.1 turns 1234.567 into 1,234.6. Ignored for text. Defaults to NULL, which writes the number as it is.

    push

    Logical. Only used when your Overleaf project syncs over git. TRUE by default, meaning the file is sent to Overleaf as soon as it's written. Set to FALSE when writing a batch of values, then call overleaf_push once at the end - it's quicker.

    Value

    The path of the file written, invisibly.

    Details

    The file ends with a %, so that LaTeX doesn't add a space after the value: \input{atlas/debt}\% gives "3.4%", not "3.4 %".

    The value is written as it is, so text containing LaTeX special characters needs escaping yourself. In particular a bare % would start a LaTeX comment, so write "50\\%" rather than "50%".

    Like grattan_save_overleaf, this writes to the project set with set_overleaf_project. If the file has been edited or deleted in Overleaf, writing it again puts your version back.

    See also

    grattan_save_overleaf to save charts the same way, overleaf_push to send batched files to Overleaf

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
set_overleaf_project("https://www.overleaf.com/project/0123456789abcdef01234567")

# At the end of a pipe
mtcars %>%
  summarise(mpg = mean(mpg)) %>%
  pull(mpg) %>%
  write_overleaf_tex("mean-mpg", accuracy = 0.1)

# Already-formatted text
write_overleaf_tex("\\$2.5 billion", "cost-total")

# Writing a batch of values: push once at the end
write_overleaf_tex(12.3, "stat-a", push = FALSE)
write_overleaf_tex(45.6, "stat-b", push = FALSE)
overleaf_push()
} # }
